title: Root cause & mitigation plan for p99 tail-latency divergence after adaptive-attn-split change
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: After the adaptive-attn-split heuristic (merged in runtime-1.20) shipped to a subset of capacity, we observed an empirical divergence in p99 tail-latency for long-context inference workloads. The median latency and throughput remained within SLOs, but p95->p99 widened by ~60% on a subset of hosts processing multi-segment prompts (seq_len > 2048) with mixed-precision kernels. This ticket captures the investigation, temporary mitigations, root cause, and concrete follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
description_2: Impact: 1) Customer-facing latency alerts triggered for two Dedicated clusters during a weekday peak window (no request loss). 2) A/B canary telemetry showed the degrading variant increased observed token-latency for a set of customer workloads using long-context summarization and conversational state. 3) No correctness or memory-corruption detected.
timeline_highlights: 2026-03-09 03:10 UTC: Canary alerting on Cluster D-A. 2026-03-09 03:25 UTC: Rollback of adaptive-attn-split patch on canary hosts reduced p99 to baseline. 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: Post-rollback analysis started; reproducer created against synthetic workload (open-source long-chat prompt).
root_cause_summary: The heuristic intended to split attention into shorter attention windows for efficiency produced a scheduling interaction: when combined with the new per-request kernel affinity mapping, certain long-context requests were fragmented with non-optimal kernel variants (mixed-precision fused-attn vs fallback slower kernel) and ended up serialized across scheduler lanes, increasing tail latency. The fallback path lacked a KV-cache warmup handshake which amplified initial token latency. In short: heuristic + affinity + missing warmup -> p99 divergence.
mitigation_taken: 1) Immediate rollback of adaptive-attn-split on canary and staged clusters. 2) Emergency hotfix: ensure affinity mapping prefers stable fused-attn kernels for seq_len > 2048. 3) Deployed temporary KV-cache warmup for fragmented requests. Alerts silenced after deployment.
action_items: - A1: Add deterministic unit and integration tests for attention-splitting + affinity interactions (owner: Arjun Patel, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-18). - A2: Add KV-cache warmup handshake to all fallback kernels and add a benchmark to catch tokenized warmup regressions (owner: Lina Gomez, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-24). - A3: Extend e2e canary test to include long-context mixed-precision workloads in CI (owner: QA team, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-21). - A4: Update scheduler to expose affinity diagnostics and conservative fallback policy behind a runtime flag (owner: Wei Zhou, estimate: 5, due: 2026-04-01). - A5: Post-release monitoring playbook and runbook updates; tie regression alerts to sample prompt set and include automatic rollback criteria (owner: SRE, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-19).
validation_plan: 1) Run a regression harness with 10k long-context requests across quant/precision variants, track p50/p95/p99. 2) Canary for 48 hours with canary traffic ramp to 10% and synthetic long-chat load. 3) Post-merge telemetry checklists: kernel-variant distributions, scheduler lane saturation, KV-cache miss rate.
testing_artifacts: Reproducer: repo://redwood/runtime/tests/long_context_repro (branch: eng/ENG-99314-repro). Benchmark dashboards: grafana://dashboards/runtime/p99-longcontext. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7642 (rollback), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7658 (affinity hotfix).
approvals_and_feedback: - PM (Ravi Singh): approves priority and customer comms. - Design: not applicable. - Security: no direct impact. - SRE (Janelle Torres): approved emergency hotfix deployment and rollback criteria.
follow_up_notes: - Surface heuristics as opt-in staging flags for at least one release cycle. - Consider moving attention-split decisions into compile-time tuning rather than runtime heuristics for critical paths. - Add a regression benchmark suite to CI that exercises scheduler+kernel interactions.
